title: Operate EMT worker and retained installation state
summary: Understand EMT configuration, readiness, worker admission, schedule intent, maintenance, backups and matched installation recovery.
use_when: EMT configuration, worker admission, readiness, installation guarantees, backups or coordinated recovery must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The goal is a product-domain intervention result or Nucleus execution authority itself.
outcome: Understand EMT configuration, readiness, worker admission, schedule intent, maintenance, backups and matched installation recovery.
effects: Configuration, admission, scheduling, maintenance, installation and activation are separate effects. Worker activation can read accounts, start authorized agent work and submit mail. Installation before initialization only installs bytes.
authority: EMT owns private configuration, incident and exchange state, admission, holds, backups and matched publication. Clockwork owns scheduling and failure halts; Nucleus owns jobs; Email owns credentials and transport.
success: Verify matched program/provider, valid configuration, known drain counts and the selected schedule, pause, hold and exact halt intent. Doctor observations do not prove receiving access or delivery.
failure_and_recovery: Retain the original migration receipt, private backup and captured operator intent. Release only the exact owned hold. Preserve unknown counts and existing halts; initialized direct selector recovery is unsupported.
privacy: Correspondence, Nucleus references, quota records and backups remain private and retained without automatic deletion. EMT stores no credentials; other providers retain separate copies. Ordinary status and logs omit bodies.
does_not_authorize: Unrequested activation, account reads, mail, another owner's hold release, implicit failure-halt approval or direct initialized selector recovery.

consumers.statement: The current user, authorized EMT worker and coordinated deployment or maintenance operator.

preconditions.statement: Initialization and maintenance require current-user state access, selected compatible dependencies and authority for the chosen operation.
New assignments require valid configured receiving domain and paths, Nucleus invocation policy two with workspace-unrestricted, and the prompt preparation prerequisites owned by emt.incident.respond.

inputs.statement: Configuration accepts the receiving domain, absolute stable Cell root, agent cwd, model and provider executable paths. Maintenance identifies the exact hold owner; migration takes a separate absolute private backup destination.

outputs.statement: Doctor returns bounded local and dependency observations with receiving permission and final delivery not_probed. Status reports retained counts. Maintenance status reports protocol_version, holds, drained and outstanding exchanges; migration returns backup evidence or backup:null when state was absent.

data_semantics.statement: Configuration, operator pause, schedule enablement, maintenance holds and failure halts are separate states. Status counts are retained records, not lifetime totals or product-health verdicts. Unknown maintenance counts are not zero.

identity_and_units.statement: emt/worker is the Clockwork binding. Holds belong to exact owners. Worker interval is 15 seconds and activation timeout is 300 seconds; schema-one domain state and release identities have separate meaning.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor describes local schema, SQLite quick_check, Clockwork interface, Nucleus health and Email executable presence at probe time. It sends no mail and submits no job. Maintenance drain advances existing exchanges without discovering new incidents or replies.
No timer-latency, service-availability, maximum recovery duration, future support lifetime or retention-horizon objective is promised.

access.statement: Supported current-user CLI and matched installer operations govern private state under ~/Library/Application Support/EMT. Explicit exchange reads and backups can expose correspondence; live activation requires separate account, investigation and email authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Init creates paused schema-one state. Configuration changes require paused and drained work. Pause stops new discovery while admitted exchanges continue; resume validates configuration and routes Clockwork EMT notifications without enabling a schedule or approving a failure halt.

The worker skips overlap and does not wait for model completion. Coordinated updates capture intent, hold and drain, retain migration evidence, install bytes and restore intent after configuration. Installation does not perform artifact-integrity, state-integrity or readiness checks. Existing pauses and failure halts survive.

Migration copies drained schema-one state and companion configuration without overwriting unmatched destinations. Recovery reuses the original backup and captured intent; direct initialized selector recovery is unsupported.

operational_limits.statement: Worker scheduling is every 15 seconds without run-at-load, with a 300-second activation timeout and overlap skipping. Ordinary Nucleus or Email unavailability is waiting; unexpected local or Clockwork interface failure ends the current pass. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks clear a pending episode. An established halt requires exact approval.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Only EMT schema one is accepted. The matched cell-install-v2 release includes binary, installer and Chancery bundle. Old pinned Clockwork brokers must be replaced before routing or running with claims.
No future support lifetime or retention horizon is promised.

reliances.statement: Clockwork owns the worker schedule, incident feed, notification checks, routing claims and failure-halt continuation.
Nucleus owns job readiness, execution and maintenance; requester-only updates leave Nucleus admission open.
Email owns receiving-account settings and credentials; deployment resolves the receiving domain through its supported interface.
Quota deferral and frozen shared-notice progress keep their independent admission and delivery rules.
